note: The Worlds layer of the Studios canon: thrones (the fiction's kings), places, pantheons, the sky and the planets. It adds no new facts of its own. Every entry names the file it is taken from, and scripts/studio-worlds-check.py fails when a cited file does not exist or does not contain the entry's name. A slot canon has not filled is status OPEN with a question in openQuestions; it is never filled with an invented name. The twelve Zodiac worlds are PROPOSED in docs/canon/zodiac-wars/BIBLE.md section 3 except Mars, Ceres and Neptune, which media.html (universe III) already fixes. Real-world kings and the real pantheons live on /kings.html and /pantheons.html and are not repeated here.

worlds.name: The Sun's corona
worlds.note: Leo's world: a house in the Sun's outer atmosphere. Shadow: truth so bright it burns the thing it shows.

worlds.name: Mercury
worlds.note: Gemini's world. Shadow: every message true to every listener, and false.

worlds.name: Venus
worlds.note: Taurus's world. Shadow: desire that owns what it loves.

worlds.name: Earth
worlds.note: Home of the Balance Court and the Solar Nexus. The proposed canon calls it the thirteenth seat: the one world the Twelve cannot rule without the consent of those who live on it.

worlds.name: The Moon
worlds.note: Cancer's world, in Earth's orbit. Shadow: protection that becomes confinement.

worlds.name: Mars
worlds.note: Aries's world; media.html: 'Ares presses Mars toward initiative'. Home of the foundry where Kael Marren is apprenticed.

worlds.name: Ceres
worlds.note: Virgo's world; media.html: 'Athena presses Ceres toward verified knowledge'. Athena's claim is why Demeter sits at Pluto.

worlds.name: Juno
worlds.note: Libra's world. Proposed only: the repository fixes Hera as Libra's god but never names her world; Juno is her Roman name. Shadow: law that outlives its reason.

worlds.name: Jupiter
worlds.note: Sagittarius's world. Shadow: authority that no longer hears a question.

worlds.name: Saturn
worlds.note: Capricorn's world. Shadow: duty kept after the family is gone.

worlds.name: Uranus
worlds.note: Aquarius's world. Shadow: invention that never asks who it is for.

worlds.name: Neptune
worlds.note: Pisces's world; media.html: 'Poseidon presses Neptune toward memory'. Home of the Deep Archive.

worlds.name: Pluto
worlds.note: Scorpio's world, moved there because Athena holds Ceres. Shadow: grief that lets the harvest rot.

places.name: The Aurelith
places.note: Seat of the Conclave. Its last day opens the film: the Conclave tries to bind the seven stones to one throne, the Guardians take them, and the sky tears (the Sundering).

places.name: The Loom
places.note: The chamber in the Aurelith where the seven stones were kept. It still answers in the present, and it offers Auren its throne.

places.name: Kharesh Basin
places.note: The excavation, directed by Hollis Reeve, with a buried temple. Placed on Earth only because its scenes are present-day.

places.name: Port Vessa
places.note: Where Auren restores objects in a museum lab and where Seraphine keeps her bookshop. Placed on Earth only because its scenes are present-day.

places.name: The Guardian Citadel
places.note: The Guardians' hold, with a statue of Ithren that wears Auren's face. Its archive intelligence is the Lamp.

places.name: The Crystal Depths
places.note: Living crystal and a two-key lock where no one hand holds the whole.

places.name: Karth Vael
places.note: The Kingdom of Ash, at the edge of the ash. Canon names a kingdom and never a ruler.

places.name: The Eternal Temple
places.note: Where Eryndor and Malachar meet in Act III, with a vault beneath it.

places.name: Ormel Hesh
places.note: A colony the Aurelith lost on the day of the Sundering; no stone is there. Today a ruined hill-fort where the afternoon repeats every eleven minutes. Season 1 episode 4, 'The Broken Kingdom'. Season 1 is not yet approved.

places.name: The Ares Foundry
places.note: Where Kael Marren is apprenticed under Orla Tevane. Oath: say the cost before the pour. The Rise of Aries is not yet approved.

places.name: Olympus Ridge
places.note: A location on Mars in the Rise of Aries package.

places.name: Meridian City
places.note: Seat of the Balance Court's Hall of the Seats, where Adaeze Okonkwo-Reyes mediates. Plain pale stone and morning daylight, so the Nexus feels uncanny beside it.

places.name: The Deep Archive
places.note: Neptune's archive, in the package's list of locations; Solenne Varr is Neptune's archivist. Blue water-light and glass tanks.

places.name: The Solar Nexus
places.note: Dormant for twelve thousand years; its reactivation starts the war. media.html fixes the reactivation. The nine rings, four doors and bell-shaped socket are from the unapproved Rise of Aries package.

places.name: The imperial capital
places.note: No document names the Empire's capital. The mood reference for it is a gold megacity of towers joined by looping rails (VISUAL_REFERENCES, batch 1).

thrones.name: The Loom's throne

holders.note: Seats himself on it during the Sundering.
The Loom offers it to him in Act III, through his mother's voice. He refuses.

thrones.note: The throne the Conclave wanted to bind all seven stones to. The film's argument is about who sits there.

thrones.name: The imperial throne
thrones.note: Galactic Thrones is the series title. The bible names an Emperor and a Princess but not their relation.

thrones.name: The throne of Queen Nefara
thrones.note: A vanished kingdom's throne. Which kingdom is not yet named.

thrones.name: The throne of the Kingdom of Ash
thrones.note: Canon names the Kingdom of Ash and no ruler.

thrones.name: The Twelve Seats of the Solar Accord
thrones.note: Twelve gods, twelve worlds, a twelve-thousand-year peace. The seats are read from the worlds list, so they cannot drift from it.

thrones.name: The thirteenth seat

holders.note: The brief's thirteenth power. Whether it claims this seat is not decided.

thrones.note: Earth belongs to no god; the Twelve cannot rule it without the consent of those who live on it. Proposed, with the Shadows, for the founder to accept or drop.

pantheons.name: The Twelve Light rulers
pantheons.note: The twelve Olympians, one per sign. Names, signs and elements are read from the canon module, not copied here. The real-world pantheons are on /pantheons.html.

pantheons.name: The Twelve Shadows
pantheons.note: Each Shadow is the same god pursued without its limit. The Regent of the Shadow Zodiac in chapter 1 is Vahn Ossara, who answers to Aries' Shadow.

pantheons.name: The four forgotten guardians
pantheons.note: Soul, Space, Void and The All: the four elements no House holds. They are conditions, not gods.

pantheons.name: The Null
pantheons.note: A collapse that has become aware. It is not the Void: it unmakes the difference between the elements.

pantheons.name: The seven original Guardians

members.basis: registry: Guardian of the Memory stone
inferred: refuses to give up his stone at the Sundering

pantheons.note: Seven Guardians took seven stones from the Loom. The registry names five as members; Eryndor and Malachar complete the seven by inference and are listed as such.

events.name: The Solar Accord
events.note: Twelve worlds bound under a twelve-thousand-year peace.

events.name: The First War
events.note: The Celestial Conflicts. The Accord paused it; the proposed canon says it was paused, not won.

events.name: The Sundering
events.note: The day the sky tears, the seven Guardians take the stones and Malachar's daughter is lost.

events.name: The Solar Nexus wakes
events.note: Saga chapter 1, 2026. The Nexus has been dormant since the Twelve divided the worlds.

rings.note: The nine-ring wall: seven rings inscribed with the seven aspects, two left blank and unnamed (conflicts C-09 and C-17). The two blanks are deliberately not filled.

openQuestions.question: Which world did the Aurelith, the Loom, the Citadel, the Crystal Depths and Karth Vael stand on, and in which age?
What is the Empire's capital called, and which world is it on?
Who rules the Kingdom of Ash, if anyone?
Does the founder accept the nine proposed worlds, the Shadows and the thirteenth seat from the Zodiac Wars bible section 3? Juno in particular is proposed, not repository canon.
Are Eryndor and Malachar the sixth and seventh Guardians, or are there two others?
How is Princess Seraya related to the imperial throne?
